newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SPENDRUPS WANTS EU TO BAN CARLSBERG/COCA COLA DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SPENDRUPS WANTS EU TO BAN CARLSBERG/COCA COLA DEAL.

text.p: A senior executive of Swedish brewer Spendrups said on Tuesday that the European Commission should not allow the planned Nordic alliance between Carlsberg and Coca Cola to go ahead.
"We are of the opinion that there would be too unequal competition," deputy managing director Ulf Spendrup told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"When two large players join forces it is clear that they become dominant."

He said Spendrups, the Swedish local partner of Pepsi Cola, had expressed its opposition to the deal in talks with the European Union executive, which is conducting a second-phase competition inquiry into the planned venture.
Asked whether Spendrups wanted the Commission to block it altogether, he said: "Yes, we think so." He said Coca Cola had sufficient resources to distribute its own goods.
EU officials refused to comment on the case, saying that no decision had yet been taken.
Pripps-Ringnes, the largest brewery in Sweden, also declined to comment. Coca Cola ended a long-running licensing agreement with Pripps-Ringnes in late 1995.
Spendrups has a licensing agreement with Pepsi Cola. It is most famous for its beers but soft drinks and mineral water account for some 40 percent of sales.
The Commission, which can force companies to change their mergers or even block them if it finds they would harm competition, is due to take a final decision by mid-September.
The EU's merger regulation bans the creation or strengthening of a dominant position on the market.

When opening its detailed inquiry in early May, the Commission said it wanted to address concerns that the venture, Coca Cola Nordic Beverages A/S, could harm competition in the Danish and Swedish soft drink markets.

The venture would join the soft drink activities of U.S. soft drink giant Coca Cola and Danish brewery group Carlsberg, first in Denmark and Sweden and eventually in the whole of the Nordic and Baltic regions.
It also involves licence agreements and a distribution joint venture with the Swedish brewer Falcon, which is jointly owned by Carlsberg and the Finnish brewing company Sinebrychoff.

The Commission noted that the two parties held 60 percent of the Danish cola market, more than 40 percent of the Danish market for non-cola soft drinks and more than 70 percent of the Swedish cola market.
Carlsberg said in early May that it believed the examination would rule in favour of the production and distribution deal with Coca Cola.

However, Ulf Spendrup said one could not only talk about the cola market as Sweden was one of few places where all brewery products were distributed in the same trucks and distribution was a central factor in the business.
"If one becomes too dominant in distribution then one will be so terribly large and efficient that it makes it more difficult for the others," he said.
Spendrup said Commission competition officials had visited Sweden as part of the investigation but that his company had not been present at an industry hearing on the case in Brussels on Monday.
